title_vi: Silas Marner, người thợ dệt ở Raveloe
translation_direction: en → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete English electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Eliot’s long ironic and reflective sentences are kept as periods, not cut into short ones; the narrator calls Godfrey anh.
decisions.rationale: The moral generalisations depend on the sentence shape.

decisions.decision: Northern village speech with light deliberate slips for Dolly and Macey instead of a regional dialect.
decisions.rationale: Eliot’s rustic voices stay distinct yet readable.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: Aaron’s line to Eppie addressed her as bác; now anh/em, ‘Em lẽ ra không cần mẹ anh bảo cũng biết thế’.
‘I won’t be over-anxious’ no longer reads as the opposite; 529, 329/338 (Priscilla is the elder sister), 540 (age 26) and 270 (cured by charm) likewise corrected.
‘mushed’ rendered as dazed or worn-out, no longer ‘humble’ (nhũn nhặn).
Eppie addresses Silas as con and bố throughout.
Christening and baptism kept distinct in Dolly’s speech.

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.source_term: the Rainbow; the Red House; the Stone-pits; Lantern Yard
glossary.draft_rendering: quán Cầu Vồng; Nhà Đỏ; hố đá; khu Lantern Yard
glossary.rationale: Fixed place names, kept the same through the book; the Stone-pits are an abandoned quarry, hố đá, distinct from mỏ đá.
Capitalised as Eliot capitalises them; Dolly’s deliberate rustic slips (thiên thằn, mô cồi, chủng đạu) mark her speech.

glossary.draft_rendering: Silas–Eppie bố/con; Dolly–Silas bác/tôi; Godfrey–Nancy anh/cô before marriage; Aaron–Eppie anh/em; Mrs Osgood mợ
glossary.rationale: Fixed kinship and class address forms keep every speaker distinct in rustic and genteel scenes.
One term for Silas’s trance fits throughout.

witness_decision: Selected the complete text of Project Gutenberg #550. Gutenberg does not identify the printed edition transcribed; the novel was first published by William Blackwood and Sons (Edinburgh and London, 1861). Not collated with a print facsimile.

unresolved_questions.explanation: Some narrator sentences remain close to the English periods; naturalness is the weakest dimension.

title_review.target_title: Silas Marner, người thợ dệt ở Raveloe
title_review.rationale: Silas Marner, người thợ dệt ở Raveloe keeps Eliot’s subtitle in Vietnamese form.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: The Wordsworth epigraph with its line breaks.
